data.name: Eusebus
data.long_meaning: The name Eusebus is derived from the Greek word eu (good) and agogos (evangelist, messenger). This name was borne by several early Christian saints, including St. Eusebius of Caesarea, who is known as the 'Father of Church History'. His extensive writings helped spread the Christian faith throughout the Roman Empire.

in_hebrew.name: אוסיבוס
in_hebrew.meaning: בעל שם טוב, מקור לטיני נוצרי
in_hebrew.long_meaning: השם אוסיבוס הוא שילוב של המילים היווניות 'אאוס' ו'ביוס', שפירושן 'טוב' ו'חיים', בהתאמה. השם מופיע בכתבי הקודש הנוצריים ומתאר אדם בעל אופי טוב ומוסר גבוה. השם משמש כזכר לנוצרים ברחבי העולם.

in_greek.name: Εὐσέβιος
in_greek.long_meaning: Τὸ ὄνομα Εὐσέβιος προέρχεται ἀπὸ τὴν ἑλληνικὴ λέξη εὐσέβεια, ἡ ὁποία σημαίνει 'εὐσεβὴς' ἤ 'σεβαστός'. Ὁ Εὐσέβιος ἦταν ἕνας τίμιος καὶ σεβασμὸς ἄνθρωπος, ποὺ ἐζούσε σύμφωνα μὲ τοὺς χριστιανικοὺς κανόνες. Ἡ ὀνομασία Εὐσέβιος ἦταν συνηθέστερη στὴν ἀρχαία Ἐκκλησία.

in_latin.name: Eusebius
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Eusebius is derived from the Greek words 'eusebeia' and 'eusebes', meaning 'piety' and 'pious' respectively. Eusebius was a common name among early Christian writers and theologians, signifying a person of great devotion and reverence to God. The name was popularized by Eusebius of Caesarea, a prominent early Christian historian and theologian.

in_english.name: Eusebus
in_english.meaning: Pious, reverent, and God-fearing Christian name
in_english.long_meaning: The name Eusebus originates from the Greek words 'eu' (εὐ) meaning 'good' and 'sebomai' (σεβόμαι) meaning 'to reverence'. It signifies a person who is deeply devoted to their faith and lives a life of piety and reverence. Eusebus was a popular name among early Christian scholars and theologians, including Eusebius of Caesarea, who wrote extensively on Christian history and theology. The name Eusebus conveys a sense of spiritual maturity, humility, and devotion to one's faith.

data.cultural_impact: St. Eusebius' works played a significant role in preserving the early history and doctrine of the Christian Church. As a prominent scholar, he contributed to the development of biblical scholarship, theological thought, and historical interpretation. His writings, which included 'The History of the Church', guided Christian communities in understanding their past and preparing for the future.

historical_references.reference: Eusebius of Caesarea was a prominent early Christian historian and theologian. He was born in Caesarea in Palestine around 260 AD and studied under Pamphilus of Caesarea. He is best known for his Ecclesiastical History, which covers the period from the apostles to the reign of Constantine in 337 AD.

Another prominent figure with the name Eusebius was Eusebius of Nicomedia. He was born in Nicomedia in Asia Minor around 260 AD and became a bishop in the late 3rd century. He was a strong supporter of the Arian heresy, which denied the divinity of Jesus Christ, and was exiled during the reign of Constantine for his beliefs. He is also known for his book Contra Constantinum, in which he defended Arianism.
